purpose: Cemiplimab-rwlc is used to treat certain types of skin cancers, including advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the skin and basal cell carcinoma. It is also used for some types of non-small cell lung cancer and cervical cancer. It is typically used when the cancer has spread or cannot be removed with surgery.
how_it_works: Your immune system has natural 'brakes' that stop it from attacking healthy cells, but cancer cells can hijack these brakes to hide from your immune system. Cemiplimab works by blocking a protein called PD-1, which releases those brakes and allows your immune system to recognize and fight the cancer cells. Think of it as taking the handcuffs off your immune system so it can do its job better.
common_side_effects: Fatigue and tiredness, skin rash or itching, diarrhea, nausea, decreased appetite, muscle or joint pain, and infections. Some people also experience changes in lab values like liver enzymes or thyroid levels.
warnings: Because this drug boosts your immune system, it can sometimes cause your immune system to attack healthy organs — this is called an immune-related reaction. This can affect your lungs, liver, intestines, kidneys, hormonal glands, or other organs and can be serious. Tell your doctor right away if you have new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, severe diarrhea, yellowing of skin or eyes, unusual weight changes, or severe fatigue. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medication can harm an unborn baby.
typical_dosing: Cemiplimab is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into a vein, usually over about 30 minutes. The typical dose is 350 mg given once every 3 weeks. Your doctor will determine exactly how many cycles you need based on how your cancer responds and how you tolerate the treatment.
